challenges.says: The first criterion (showing the key/value reading so it can be corrected) cites no rule and its wording does not say why; it states behaviour that no rule or decision gives, and the reason sits only in the open list, not in the criteria.

The title and step say the terms are judged as the person types, but the empty-terms and root-key criteria (from the cited rules) fire only when the person asks to search, so the story promises more than its criteria deliver.

The last criterion (matching policies are shown without a separate request step) cites no rule and does not say why it has none; it invents behaviour that no rule or decision states and contradicts the cited rule that a search starts when asked.
